corrections: The saved row timestamp follows the blocking HX711 read, whereas the RPM value was queried earlier. The gap is not recorded and cannot be exactly corrected retrospectively.
Existing RPM fitted delays and time constants can include transport timing, variable row-time assignment error and sparse sampling. They are descriptive fits, not identified physical motor constants.
Existing crossing brackets are brackets on row time, not rigorous bounds on actual RPM measurement or rotor response time.
HX711 output rate alone is not a universal hard 0.3-second identifiability cutoff. Timing accuracy, input scheduling, repeatability, sensor dynamics and model assumptions also matter.
Similar up/down thrust response may be influenced by load-cell/fixture dynamics. An axial force trace alone cannot separate that from motor/propeller dynamics.
before_more_transient_tests: Acquire RPM independently of HX711, using a single owner for serial transactions.
Log each command write start/acknowledgement, RPM request/reply interval, and HX711 ready/read-complete timestamps separately.
Check achievable RPM cadence and telemetry freshness with safety monitoring enabled during the next supervised moderate-power run.
Retain battery/status, force-range, force-limit, stale-sensor and stop-on-error handling; use variable dwell timing to avoid sampling all repeated edges at one phase.
